title: Manifold-Optimal Guidance: A Unified Riemannian Control View of Diffusion Guidance
claim: Naive Euclidean guidance shortcuts off the data manifold; a geometry-aware update stays on-manifold while still converging efficiently toward the condition.
layout: 3 panels: large toy manifold left, two stacked line plots right
description: The left panel is a large 2-D toy picture. A gray spiral tube of high-density data fades out toward its edges, with dashed lines marking the manifold. A black start dot sits at the center and a green star marks the condition near the upper left. Three colored trajectories with arrowheads leave the start. The red one (CFG, Euclidean) cuts straight to the star and leaves the manifold. The orange one (APG, projected) loops along the manifold more slowly. The blue one (MOG, ours) heads toward the star while staying close to the manifold. A legend sits at the bottom right. The right side has two stacked line plots over 120 steps. The top plot, 'Off-Manifold Artifacts', shows distance to the manifold, with red spiking and blue staying smooth and low. The bottom plot, 'Convergence Speed (Energy)', shows conditional energy, with red dropping fastest, blue next and orange slowest. Red, orange and blue are used consistently across all panels. The eye goes first to the spiral and the colored arrows.
caption: Toy spiral manifold illustration of guidance geometry. Left: trajectories on a high-density spiral tube. Standard CFG (red) takes a Euclidean shortcut that leaves the manifold. A projected update (orange) stays closer to the manifold but progresses more slowly. MOG (blue) follows a geometry-aware direction that remains near the manifold while moving efficiently toward the condition. Top right: distance to the manifold over steps, highlighting off-manifold deviation under CFG. Bottom right: conditional energy over steps, showing that MOG reduces energy rapidly without leaving the high-density region.
abstract: Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) serves as the de facto control mechanism for conditional diffusion, yet high guidance scales notoriously induce oversaturation, texture artifacts, and structural collapse. We attribute this failure to a geometric mismatch: standard CFG performs Euclidean extrapolation in ambient space, inadvertently driving sampling trajectories off the high-density data manifold. To resolve this, we present Manifold-Optimal Guidance (MOG), a framework that reformulates guidance as a local optimal control problem. MOG yields a closed-form, geometry-aware Riemannian update that corrects off-manifold drift without requiring retraining. Leveraging this perspective, we further introduce Auto-MOG, a dynamic energy-balancing schedule that adaptively calibrates guidance strength, effectively eliminating the need for manual hyperparameter tuning. Extensive validation demonstrates that MOG yields superior fidelity and alignment compared to baselines, with virtually no added computational overhead.
